title: Wren and the Hollow
premise: Tamsin Kavanagh, last apprentice of the Wayfarers' Guild, guides travelers through the Thornfell mountains by routes only his guild remembers. When a mortally wounded stranger dies in his arms clutching a map of Aldermere—a country that was erased from the world two hundred years ago—Tamsin discovers the map is waking inside his own blood, and that he carries the stranger's memories along with it. Hunted by the Crown's Inquisitors, who erased Aldermere to hide their own founding crime, and shadowed by Wren, a sharp-tongued refugee who claims to be the last living child of that vanished land, Tamsin must retrace the map to the Hollow, the door out of a country that no longer exists. In the climax he learns he is himself an Aldermere child, smuggled out as an infant, and that opening the Hollow will either restore Aldermere at the cost of every life now built on its absence—or let the dead country finally rest. Tamsin chooses to let it rest, keeping only its memory, and finds that the family he made on the road is the home he was always seeking.
about_author: J. M. Pemberton is the pen name of a former cartographer's assistant who spent a decade drawing borders that history kept redrawing. They write fantasy about the people who live in the margins of maps, and live in a house full of atlases and one unreasonably opinionated cat.

chapters.title: The Last Apprentice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The Wayfarers' Guild is down to four members and a leaking roof; Tamsin guides a merchant caravan through the Thornfells and returns to find the Guildmaster selling the guildhall. The beat is weary pride—Tamsin loves the roads even as the world stops needing them.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the Grey Stair
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. On the treacherous Grey Stair pass, Tamsin finds a man bleeding out from a wound that doesn't bleed right, pressed through with faint silver script. The stranger presses a folded map into Tamsin's hands and dies saying, 'Take it to the Hollow.' Beat: dread and unwilling obligation.

chapters.title: What the Map Wants
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The map won't burn, tear, or be put down—it reappears in Tamsin's pocket and its ink shifts when he sleeps, showing him roads he's never walked. The Guildmaster orders it destroyed. Beat: creeping realization that the map has chosen him, not the reverse.

chapters.title: Wren of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, a refugee pickpocket working the border town of Marrowgate, spots Tamsin's map and recognizes the shape of Aldermere—the country her grandmother sang about. She lifts it, is caught, and instead of turning her in, Tamsin asks her what she knows. Beat: wary, electric first alliance.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Summons
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Crown Inquisitor Serle Halvane arrives at the guildhall, polite and terrible, asking after a dead man and a missing map. Tamsin lies for the first time in his honest life and feels the guild's safety crack around him. Beat: fear sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: Roads Out of the World
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Tamsin and Wren flee north on smugglers' roads, and Wren teaches him Aldermere's songs while the map teaches him its roads. They discover the map's script is the same silver writing on the dead stranger. Beat: the found-family bond begins, tender and unspoken.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the village of Bellharbour, saying Aldermere's name aloud makes lamps gutter and old people weep. Wren learns her grandmother was a Hollow-keeper, and that the family lullaby is a key. Beat: grief for a heritage she never got to hold.

chapters.title: Halvane's Hounds
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Inquisitor Halvane unleashes the hounds—men remade with the same silver script, scentless and tireless. Tamsin uses a guild trick to break trail but is wounded, and Wren's clumsy field-stitching becomes an accidental confession of care. Beat: the cost of running becomes real.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Grave
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The map leads them to the grave of Aldermere's last royal cartographer, who was buried alive with his work. In the coffin-crypt they find his journal: the country wasn't conquered, it was folded out of the world by treaty—and the Inquisition guards the fold. Beat: the scale of the lie revealed.

chapters.title: A House That Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sheltering in an inn that stands where an Aldermere farmhouse used to be, Wren dreams the farmhouse's memories and wakes weeping for people she never met. Tamsin, holding her, realizes he dreamed the same room. Beat: intimacy deepening into something neither will name.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Road
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They recruit Brannic, an ex-Wayfarer who sold guild secrets to the Crown years ago and now wants absolution. Tamsin must decide whether a traitor can be trusted with the map. Beat: bitter forgiveness—found family includes the ones who failed you.

chapters.title: What the Stranger Left
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The silver script spreads from Tamsin's wound into his veins, and with it come the dead stranger's memories: a mother's kitchen, a border crossing, an infant handed over the fold. Tamsin realizes the memories are his own. Beat: identity shattered and reformed.

chapters.title: The Hollow-Keepers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the mountain shrine of Vael they find three surviving Hollow-keepers, ancient and half-forgotten, who confirm it: Tamsin was smuggled out of Aldermere as the fold closed, and the stranger who died on the Grey Stair was the smuggler coming back for him. Beat: fury and vertigo—his whole life was an exit wound.

chapters.title: The Price of a Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The keepers explain the choice: open the Hollow and Aldermere returns, displacing the towns and people built on its absence; let it rest and the last Aldermere blood—Tamsin—must stand at the door and close it from the inside, unmaking the script in his veins. Beat: duty and love set on a collision course.

chapters.title: Serle Halvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Halvane's POV, the only chapter from the antagonist. Halvane reveals the Inquisition's founders committed the original atrocity that forced Aldermere's folding, and that he has spent his life guarding the lie because the truth would burn the Crown down. Beat: the enemy made human, and more dangerous for it.

chapters.title: The Siege of Vael
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Halvane's hounds and soldiers storm the shrine. Brannic dies holding the stair, the keepers are scattered, and Tamsin uses every smuggler's road he knows to get Wren and the map out through a collapsing passage. Beat: grief, sacrifice, and the guild's knowledge made holy at last.

chapters.title: Where the Map Ends
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The map's final road leads down beneath the Thornfells to a door of grey stone carved with the lullaby's melody in silver script. Wren sings it, and the door wakes. Beat: awe edged with terror—the Hollow is real, and it knows their names.

chapters.title: The Country Under the World
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Through the door lies Aldermere, folded and frozen: harvest fields mid-motion, a kitchen with bread still rising, the stranger's mother's chair. Tamsin walks his own erased childhood and understands what restoration would cost the living. Beat: heartbreak and homesickness for a home that never got to exist.

chapters.title: Halvane at the Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Halvane arrives with the remnant of his hounds, demanding the door be sealed and the truth buried forever; Wren stands between him and Tamsin and refuses to move. The confrontation turns on whether a country can be built on a lie and still be worth saving. Beat: the moral climax, blades and arguments both drawn.

chapters.title: Let the Dead Country Rest
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin chooses neither restoration nor Halvane's burial of truth: he opens the Hollow wide, lets Aldermere's people and memory pour out as story, song, and witness into the world—then sings the closing verse and unmakes the door, the script, and the stranger's lingering grip on him. Beat: the climax's release—grief transmuted into testament.

chapters.title: The Truth, Unfolded
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Aldermere's story spreads like weather; towns learn what stands where the old farms stood, the Crown's founding lie cracks, and Halvane, broken, chooses to testify rather than die for the secret. Wren is claimed by no nation and claims herself. Beat: justice arriving quietly, without conquest.

chapters.title: A Guild of Our Own
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, epilogue. A year on, Tamsin reopens the guildhall—not as the Wayfarers' last outpost, but as a school where refugees, cartographers, and singers map the world together, Aldermere's roads remembered in ink instead of blood. Wren hangs the restored map by the door. Beat: home was never a country; it's the people who walk beside you.
